Pasighat does have a documented Hindu temple landscape: the Dangaria Baba Shiv Mandir at Ranaghat (regarded locally as the town's oldest Shiva temple), a Shiv Mandir listed at Pasighat town centre, the Pasighat Assamese Namghar, a Gorkha Shiva Mandir-cum-Community Hall inaugurated at 2 Mile in September 2026, plus the town's only Buddhist worship place (Pasighat Buddhist Temple) and a gurudwara; there is also an Akashi Ganga Mandir (a Shakti peetha with a sacred kund) at Likabali in Lower Siang, but that is a different place ~75 km away and is not in Pasighat. name: Ganga Mandir
town_description: Pasighat (approx. 28.067 N, 95.327 E) is the headquarters of East Siang district, situated on the west bank of the Siang river where it enters the Assam plains. It is the oldest town of Arunachal Pradesh, known for the Siang river front, Komlighat, the Pasighat Buddhist Temple, the East Siang District Museum and the Dangaria Baba Shiv Mandir at Ranaghat.

travel.airport: Pasighat Airport, a military airstrip upgraded for civilian use, on the edge of town.
travel.railway: Murkeong Sel is the nearest railhead (sources cite it ~18-19 km from the Dangaria Baba temple area); the nearest major junctions are in Assam (Tinsukia/Dibrugarh).
travel.road: Pasighat is on NH-13 and is well connected by road to Assam and the rest of Arunachal Pradesh.

visitor_information.best_time: Winter (October to March) is generally the pleasantest season in the Pasighat plains.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not verifiable for this record; town temples typically open at dawn and close in the evening.
